# rnndescent

An R package for approximate nearest neighbor search on dense and sparse
data. Use it to build a neighbor graph, refine an existing graph, or
build an index to query with new data.

The package adapts the core search methods from Leland McInnes’s
[PyNNDescent](https://github.com/lmcinnes/pynndescent) to R. It uses
[nearest neighbor descent](https://doi.org/10.1145/1963405.1963487) and
[random partition trees](https://doi.org/10.1145/1374376.1374452). It
also draws on [FANNG](https://doi.org/10.1109/CVPR.2016.616) and
[NGT](https://github.com/yahoojapan/NGT).

## Current Status

**26 May 2026.** Version 0.2.0 adds the Haversine metric and improves
input validation. [CRAN
release](https://cran.r-project.org/package=rnndescent)

## Installation

### CRAN

``` r

install.packages("rnndescent")
```

### Development version

``` r

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("jlmelville/rnndescent")
```

Building from source requires a C++17 compiler. See [Rtools for
Windows](https://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/Rtools/) and the [R
build tools for macOS](https://mac.r-project.org/tools/).

## Example

``` r

library(rnndescent)

set.seed(42)
x <- iris[1:4]

# Find the 15 nearest neighbors of each observation
iris_knn <- rnnd_knn(x, k = 15)

# Build an index on reference rows and query it with the remaining rows
iris_index <- rnnd_build(x[1:100, ], k = 15)
iris_query_nn <- rnnd_query(iris_index, x[101:150, ], k = 15)
```

## Missing Metrics

The `metric` argument takes the name of a built-in distance. This covers
many PyNNDescent metrics, with gaps such as Mahalanobis and weighted
Minkowski. See the [metrics
article](https://jlmelville.github.io/rnndescent/articles/metrics.html)
for the full list.

## Citation

Dong, W., Moses, C., & Li, K. (2011, March). Efficient k-nearest
neighbor graph construction for generic similarity measures. In
*Proceedings of the 20th international conference on World wide web*
(pp. 577-586). ACM.
[doi.org/10.1145/1963405.1963487](https://doi.org/10.1145/1963405.1963487).

# Package index

## Main interface

Find approximate neighbors or build and query an index.

- [`rnnd_knn()`](https://jlmelville.github.io/rnndescent/reference/rnnd_knn.md)
  : Find approximate nearest neighbors
- [`rnnd_build()`](https://jlmelville.github.io/rnndescent/reference/rnnd_build.md)
  : Build approximate nearest neighbors index and neighbor graph
- [`rnnd_prepare()`](https://jlmelville.github.io/rnndescent/reference/rnnd_prepare.md)
  : Prepare an index for repeated queries
- [`rnnd_query()`](https://jlmelville.github.io/rnndescent/reference/rnnd_query.md)
  : Query an index for approximate nearest neighbors

## Individual search methods

Find or query neighbors using brute force, random selection, nearest
neighbor descent, or random projection forests.

- [`brute_force_knn()`](https://jlmelville.github.io/rnndescent/reference/brute_force_knn.md)
  : Find exact nearest neighbors by brute force
- [`brute_force_knn_query()`](https://jlmelville.github.io/rnndescent/reference/brute_force_knn_query.md)
  : Query exact nearest neighbors by brute force
- [`random_knn()`](https://jlmelville.github.io/rnndescent/reference/random_knn.md)
  : Find nearest neighbors by random selection
- [`random_knn_query()`](https://jlmelville.github.io/rnndescent/reference/random_knn_query.md)
  : Query nearest neighbors by random selection
- [`nnd_knn()`](https://jlmelville.github.io/rnndescent/reference/nnd_knn.md)
  : Find nearest neighbors using nearest neighbor descent
- [`rpf_knn()`](https://jlmelville.github.io/rnndescent/reference/rpf_knn.md)
  : Find nearest neighbors using a random projection forest
- [`rpf_build()`](https://jlmelville.github.io/rnndescent/reference/rpf_build.md)
  : Create a random projection forest nearest neighbor index
- [`rpf_knn_query()`](https://jlmelville.github.io/rnndescent/reference/rpf_knn_query.md)
  : Query a random projection forest index for nearest neighbors
- [`rpf_filter()`](https://jlmelville.github.io/rnndescent/reference/rpf_filter.md)
  : Keep the best trees in a random projection forest

## Graph search and utilities

Prepare and query search graphs, merge neighbor graphs, and assess their
properties.

- [`prepare_search_graph()`](https://jlmelville.github.io/rnndescent/reference/prepare_search_graph.md)
  : Convert a nearest neighbor graph into a search graph
- [`graph_knn_query()`](https://jlmelville.github.io/rnndescent/reference/graph_knn_query.md)
  : Query a search graph for nearest neighbors
- [`merge_knn()`](https://jlmelville.github.io/rnndescent/reference/merge_knn.md)
  : Merge multiple approximate nearest neighbors graphs
- [`k_occur()`](https://jlmelville.github.io/rnndescent/reference/k_occur.md)
  : Quantify hubness of a nearest neighbor graph
- [`neighbor_overlap()`](https://jlmelville.github.io/rnndescent/reference/neighbor_overlap.md)
  : Overlap between the indices of two nearest neighbor graphs
- [`truncate_knn()`](https://jlmelville.github.io/rnndescent/reference/knn-utilities.md)
  [`sort_knn()`](https://jlmelville.github.io/rnndescent/reference/knn-utilities.md)
  [`remove_self_knn()`](https://jlmelville.github.io/rnndescent/reference/knn-utilities.md)
  [`self_first_knn()`](https://jlmelville.github.io/rnndescent/reference/knn-utilities.md)
  : Manipulate nearest neighbor graphs
- [`knn_to_sparse()`](https://jlmelville.github.io/rnndescent/reference/knn_to_sparse.md)
  : Convert a neighbor graph to a sparse matrix
- [`knn_distances()`](https://jlmelville.github.io/rnndescent/reference/knn_distances.md)
  : Calculate distances for fixed neighbor indices
